section: Space policy and commercialisation - Indian Space Policy 2023, IN-SPACe, NSIL, private launch sector

accepted.s: On 18 July 2026, which achievement was associated with Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-1?
o: India's first reusable orbital vehicle launch
India's first private orbital rocket launch
India's first private sub-orbital rocket launch
accepted.x: Vikram-1 became India's first private orbital rocket on 18 July 2026. Vikram-S had earlier been India's first private rocket, but it was not the first private orbital launch.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact achievement associated with the named vehicle.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Vikram-S from Vikram-1?
o: Vikram-S was the first private rocket, whereas Vikram-1 was the first private orbital rocket.
Vikram-S was launched in 2026, whereas Vikram-1 was launched in 2022.
Vikram-S carried the first NSIL demand-driven mission, whereas Vikram-1 was a satellite.
Vikram-S was the first private orbital rocket, whereas Vikram-1 was the first government-owned rocket.
accepted.x: Vikram-S was India's first private rocket in 2022, while Vikram-1 became India's first private orbital rocket in 2026. The two achievements and years should not be interchanged.
accepted.tq: Separate two similar names by comparing their distinct milestones and years.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Skyroot Aerospace
(b) Vikram-1
(c) VIT-AP
(d) Sriharikota

List-II
(i) Location of India's only operational spaceport
(ii) Payload flown on a private orbital rocket
(iii) Hyderabad-based private space company
(iv) India's first private orbital rocket

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
accepted.x: Skyroot Aerospace is based in Hyderabad; Vikram-1 is India's first private orbital rocket; a VIT-AP payload flew on Vikram-1; and Sriharikota is India's only operational spaceport.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure location pair and then eliminate codes using the remaining unique associations.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the issues raised in debates on India's private space sector:
1. India does not yet have a Space Activities Act.
2. More than 90% of space-grade semiconductors are imported.
3. There is no sovereign-backed insurance for long-gestation space ventures.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements describe concerns associated with India's space-sector ecosystem: the absence of a Space Activities Act, dependence on imported space-grade chips exceeding 90%, and the lack of sovereign-backed insurance for long-gestation ventures.
accepted.tq: Test all statements against the three separate policy and industrial constraints.

accepted.s: In the context of India's space activities, the figure of 18 refers to the number of:
o: private orbital rockets launched by India in 2025
collision-avoidance manoeuvres carried out in LEO in 2025
space-grade semiconductor plants established in India in 2025
accepted.x: Eighteen collision-avoidance manoeuvres were carried out in low Earth orbit in 2025, reflecting the growing problem of LEO congestion.
accepted.tq: Attach the numerical figure to its precise operational context rather than to a nearby space-sector statistic.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly described as India's only operational spaceport?
accepted.x: Sriharikota is India's only operational spaceport. Tirupati Space City is a future-oriented development that builds on the existing Sriharikota base.
accepted.tq: Use the unique-location clue and distinguish an operational facility from a proposed or developing project.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Vikram-S becomes India's first private rocket.
B. Eighteen collision-avoidance manoeuvres are recorded in LEO.
C. Vikram-1 becomes India's first private orbital rocket.

Select the correct sequence.
accepted.x: Vikram-S achieved the first-private-rocket milestone in 2022, the 18 LEO collision-avoidance manoeuvres were recorded in 2025, and Vikram-1 achieved the first-private-orbital-rocket milestone in 2026.
accepted.tq: Place the dated milestones first and then verify the sequence from 2022 through 2026.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements best reflects the emerging institutional debate after Vikram-1's achievement?
o: Sriharikota has ceased to be India's operational spaceport.
The role of ISRO is being debated in relation to the growing participation of private industry.
Private companies have been prohibited from undertaking orbital launches.
India has become fully self-reliant in space-grade semiconductors.
accepted.x: The success of Vikram-1 intensified debate over the future role of ISRO vis-à-vis the expanding private space industry. The other statements contradict the identified conditions.
accepted.tq: Apply the achievement to the institutional issue it is understood to have intensified.
